consequence.statement: Package installation commands that rely on the --registry flag to specify a default registry will fail in Crossplane v2.0.0; fully qualified package URLs must be provided explicitly.

original.statement: Crossplane v2.0.0 removes the --registry CLI flag, requiring users to always specify fully qualified URLs when installing packages instead of relying on a default registry value.

decision.reason: The question is about the removal of native patch and transform composition, but the proposed consequence covers a different change: dropping the `--registry` flag. [ev-792eae516f7e] lists five separate breaking changes in one passage (patch-and-transform, ControllerConfig, external secret stores, XR connection details and the default registry), so one consequence can't cover them all. The kind is also not supported: the evidence says only that fully qualified package URLs are now required. It does not say the upgrade or install fails, so upgrade-blocked overstates it. For patch-and-transform itself, the evidence says only that it is removed and replaced by composition functions. It doesn't say what happens to existing Compositions, so no corrected consequence follows from this evidence.
